name: How long is this Everest Base Camp Trek?

acceptedAnswer.text: This package is 14 calendar days from Kathmandu arrival to final departure. Days 2–12 include walking and the two acclimatization hikes. Extra contingency days are outside the advertised schedule.

name: How high are Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar?

acceptedAnswer.text: Everest Base Camp is approximately 5,364 m. The itinerary uses approximately 5,545 m for Kala Patthar, its highest scheduled viewpoint. Gorak Shep, around 5,164 m, is the highest overnight stop.

name: Can I see Everest from Base Camp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Base Camp does not provide the classic unobstructed summit panorama. Kala Patthar is the main viewpoint included for the familiar Everest perspective, when conditions permit.

name: Can a beginner do this trek?

acceptedAnswer.text: A well-prepared beginner may be suitable. You need endurance for consecutive mountain days, realistic expectations about teahouses and cold, and a willingness to follow the acclimatization plan. Discuss your readiness with the team.

name: Do I need climbing experience?

acceptedAnswer.text: The standard route is a non-technical trek. It does not include rope climbing or technical glacier travel. High altitude and sustained walking still make it demanding.

name: Can I book a private trek or join as a solo traveler?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the supplied article describes group and private guided arrangements. Confirm the price, departure status and any supplement, particularly if nobody else books the date.

name: When should I go?

acceptedAnswer.text: Spring and autumn are the main planning choices. Your preferred scenery, tolerance for cold, crowd preference and flight flexibility determine the most suitable departure.

name: Can children or older adults join?

acceptedAnswer.text: Suitability is individual. Health, preparation, previous altitude experience, ability to report symptoms and itinerary flexibility matter more than age alone. Discuss family or senior requirements before booking.

name: Can I add Gokyo, a peak climb or more time in Nepal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the article describes those options, but mountain extensions need a revised itinerary and peak climbs need separate climbing arrangements. Keep a flight buffer before fixed onward travel.

name: Is a guide included, and what about permits?

acceptedAnswer.text: The source package includes a licensed guide and applicable permits. NTB’s published revised route list includes EBC under its guide/TIMS provisions, and Khumbu operates local registration. Confirm the exact documents in your booking.

name: Will I fly from Kathmandu or Ramechhap?

acceptedAnswer.text: The departure airport depends on the operating arrangements for your dates. The team should confirm the airport, pickup and transfer plan before the flight day.

name: What happens if the Lukla flight is delayed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The team reviews rebooking and itinerary options according to actual conditions. Extra nights or replacement transport may cost more. Confirm the delay policy and leave contingency time.

name: How much luggage can my porter carry?

acceptedAnswer.text: The draft describes about 20 kg per porter and a common shared arrangement for two trekkers. Confirm your personal allowance, the crew’s equipment allowance and the exact ratio in writing; do not treat the maximum as a packing target.

name: What should stay in my daypack?

acceptedAnswer.text: Water, snacks, warm and waterproof layers, sun protection, headlamp, essential medication, passport, money, electronics and other items you need before the next lodge. Your porter may be walking ahead.

name: Can I return by helicopter?

acceptedAnswer.text: A separately arranged helicopter return may shorten the descent. Confirm the price, pickup, baggage and weather backup. It does not remove the need to acclimatize on the ascent.

name: What should I confirm before booking?

acceptedAnswer.text: The exact itinerary, group/private basis, guide and porter arrangement, permits, flights, accommodation, meals, live price, deposit, exclusions, cancellation terms, emergency support and delay-related costs.

name: What accommodation should I expect?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kathmandu hotels and mountain teahouses, normally twin-sharing. Facilities become more basic higher up, and a private room or attached bathroom is not guaranteed at every stop.

name: Are meals included, and can I eat vegetarian food?

acceptedAnswer.text: The standard source package includes breakfast, lunch and dinner during trekking. Vegetarian dishes are common. Declare allergies, vegan requirements and other restrictions beforehand; menu choice and preparation vary.

name: How do I manage drinking water?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use treated water and a suitable purification method. Reusable bottles are practical. Ask about local boiled or filtered water and its cost, and protect bottles from freezing higher up.

name: Will Wi-Fi, charging and hot showers be available?

acceptedAnswer.text: They may be available for additional fees at some lodges, but service and reliability vary. Carry a power bank and download essential information offline.

name: Why are there two acclimatization days?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Namche and Dingboche stops allow time to adapt and usually include a controlled hike followed by a return to the same sleeping elevation. They should not be removed simply to shorten the trip.

name: What if I develop altitude symptoms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell your guide immediately and do not continue ascending with symptoms. The response may include rest, assessment, descent and medical care. Severe or worsening symptoms need urgent help.

name: What insurance should I arrange?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check that your policy covers the actual planned trekking altitude, medical treatment and appropriate helicopter evacuation. Review exclusions, pre-existing conditions and the authorization procedure directly with your insurer.

name: Is helicopter evacuation guaranteed?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Medical need, weather, daylight, aircraft availability and suitable landing conditions affect evacuation. Insurance coverage does not guarantee an aircraft can operate immediately.

name: How should I handle cash and tipping?

acceptedAnswer.text: Prepare Nepali rupees in Kathmandu, with smaller notes and an emergency reserve. Ask for current crew tipping guidance and clarify group distribution. Mountain ATMs and card payments should not be your main plan.
